analysis.title: US Equities Mid-Day Color - GS Equities Mid-Day Color 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: Major indices rallied hard after the midterm elections, which removed an event risk. SPX was up 185bps and retook its 50-day moving average at 7693. NDX was up 155bps, with AAPL, MSFT and AMZN accounting for about 65% of the move.
WTI fell 8.5%, its largest one-day percentage decline since May 20, when Trump postponed strikes on Tehran's energy infrastructure.

The desk sees a rotation into hyperscalers (GSX1MEGA, +350bps) funded by selling semiconductors (SOX, -250bps). The desk's reasoning is that if compute is scarce because capacity cannot be added, it can be sold at a higher price, and if capacity cannot be built, companies spend less, which may lead to renewed buybacks.
The AI complex stayed under pressure: AI Leaders (GSTMTAIL) -500bps, Power Up America (GSENEPOW) -600bps, Data centers (GSTMTDAT) -540bps.

Consumer Discretionary (GSXUCOND, +530bps) and Staples (GSXUSTAP, +430bps) both moved more than 3 standard deviations. The desk attributes this to positioning, lower rates, lower oil and a view of less pressure on spending from future budget and debt negotiations. Homebuilders (GSXUBLDR) rose 7% as rate-sensitive names worked.

GIR's view on the midterms is that larger-than-expected majorities could give Democrats slightly more leverage with the White House but will dilute small factions within the caucus. GIR expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to try to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse last year's spending cuts.

Liquidity was thin and volatile. ETFs were 29% of volume (28% YTD average). Exchange volumes were up 25% vs the 5-day average while top-of-book liquidity was down 30% at $6.12mm on the touch. The S&P e-mini intraday band was 3.2%, the highest in 7 months.

Desk flows: activity was 6 out of 10 in the pockets most affected by the midterms, and the desk was 2% better to buy overall. Long-only and hedge fund clients were slightly better to buy on modest numbers. Info Tech had a large sell skew for the 5th straight day, with net selling of -$1.5bn on the day. The desk sold Health Care, Utilities and REITs and bought ETFs and hyperscalers.
Chart of the Day: 21 GS baskets had moves above 3 sigma, the most since June 5 and the second most over a 1-year lookback.

GSXUCOND rose 530bps, a 3+ standard deviation move, on positioning, lower rates and lower oil. Homebuilders rose 7%.
GSXUSTAP rose 430bps, a 3+ standard deviation move, on the same drivers as discretionary.
The desk had a large sell skew for the 5th day in a row, with net selling of -$1.5bn on the day.
